messages:
deploy-bot: Kicking staged rollout v6.1.0 -> 15% across us-west-2 and ap-northeast-1. Change window 04:00-06:00 UTC. Health checks: 15m error-rate, p99 memory, GC pauses. Release notes: <internal/release/6.1.0>

lina: Heads up, perf team flagged increased memory usage in the model-serving container on the canary fleet after ~6m. p99 mem jumped from 1.8GB -> 3.2GB. No OOMs yet but GC pauses increasing.

raj: I see OOM kills on one canary host in ap-northeast-1 at 04:08 UTC. Container restarted with exit code 137. Stack shows memory spike during large-batch decoding.

taylor: We did bump max_batch_size in this release to improve throughput (was 32 -> 64). That could explain it. There was an optimization to hold KV cache longer which may increase resident set.

infra-bot: Note: autoscaler will attempt to replace the killed container; if we keep ramping the higher batch will push more load. Recommend pausing.

oncall-bot: @raj, @taylor 1: oncall is grace. Pager notified.

grace: Oncall here. Quick triage: are the OOMs isolated to one node or visible across canaries? If single node it could be a node-level leak, if many then regression in release.

raj: Logs show 4 OOM events across 3 hosts in ap-northeast and 2 in us-west-2 within 10m. Not isolated. Repro by running 200 concurrent decode with max_batch_size=64.

lina: Repro steps in gist: `python tools/load_model.py --concurrency 200 --batch-size 64 --seq 1024`. Results in steady growth and eventual OOM within ~3m.

taylor: Given repro and code change, I'd recommend PAUSE rollout, PIN affected regions back to v6.0.3, and open hotfix to revert batch-size bump and revert KV retention tweak. Alternative: toggle a runtime flag to force batch_size=32 for now. Which is faster?

lina: We don't have a runtime knob for KV retention, but we do have a runtime cap override for batch size. I can push a config change to fleet to cap at 32 immediately — faster than full rollback. But pinning routes still safer to stop traffic shift.

grace: Action plan: 1) pause rollout to prevent further percent increases; 2) pin us-west-2 and ap-northeast-1 to v6.0.3; 3) apply runtime cap batch_size=32 across canaries to stop new OOMs; 4) create hotfix branch to remove KV retention change and run staging stress; 5) only unpin after staging validated.

raj: Commands:
```
# pause rollout
deployctl rollout pause --version=6.1.0 --strategy=percent
# pin regions
deployctl pin --version=6.0.3 --routes=us-west-2,ap-northeast-1 --reason="memory spike / OOMs"
# apply runtime cap (infra config)
infractl set cluster-config --key=model.batch_size.cap --value=32 --scope=canary
```

Taylor: I approve the cap + pin. Applying cap now while grace runs pause/pin.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused by grace (exec-20260324-201). No further percent increases will be applied.

deploy-bot: Pins applied: us-west-2 -> v6.0.3, ap-northeast-1 -> v6.0.3.

infra-bot: Cluster config updated: model.batch_size.cap=32 (applied to canary pools).

raj: Confirming reduction in memory growth on newly spawned containers after cap. No new OOMs in last 6m. Existing restarted containers still finishing warmup.

lina: Creating incident INC-20260324-12 and assigning taylor + raj for hotfix. Hotfix strategy: revert KV retention change and add mem-pressure tests to CI. ETA ~40m for PR + staging run.

grace: Decision summary: STOP further rollout. Pin affected regions to stable. Apply runtime batch cap to stop immediate risk. Hotfix + staging verification required before any GO. We'll reconvene in 40m or when staging results in.

taylor: I'll open the revert PR and start staging stress test once merged. Will post green/red here.

deploy-bot: Thread paused. Use `deployctl` or @grace to reopen for GO.
